column1: # §30 (review 13 blocker 2): the shapes a send prompt's punctuation gives a file name.
# One row per line: what a prompt says, a tab, then the names kit check reads from it
# (space-separated; nothing after the tab when it names none). Read against a repo
# holding Makefile, meta/A.md, .gitignore and the directory src/hands, with a kit
# plain, and every quote the handbook's prompts use (ASCII and Unicode)
# a line, a column, an anchor
# bare relative names: a caps name, a build-file name, a file the repo has
# false positives: prose the bare-name rule reads as a file name (§31, review 14
# should-fix 6). The class is fail-closed — the prompt fails kit check until the
# repository has that file — and no shipped prompt says one of these. Pinned here
# so a change to the rule that widens or narrows the class is a fixture diff.
# the words next to them that stay prose: VERDICT is excepted by name
# this repository's and the templates' send prompts, verbatim

Read meta/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md and review mission {n} of this repository: every commit after the last review: commit on origin/main (the protocol says how to find the base). Follow the protocol exactly, commit only meta/reviews/REVIEW-{n}.md, and begin your reply with the VERDICT line it specifies.
Review WORKPLAN.md commits since the last review: commit on this branch, per WORKPLAN.md §0.2. Begin your reply with: VERDICT: review run {n} blockers=<k> should-fix=<m>
